metric.semantic_density.fact_state_source: Per-probe frozen site_id list taken directly from semantic_site_matrix.json language_templates.Quidra.site_order for each probe; EXPLICIT_LOCAL/NONLOCAL/IMPLICIT/ABSENT assignments made per the evidence-state definitions in semantic_compression.md 6.1.3, applied identically to Quidra as would be applied to any other language given the same local surface form.
metric.semantic_density.methodology_basis: benchmark/template/methodology/semantic_compression.md section 6.1.3.A: raw value = explicit local semantic sites (EXPLICIT_LOCAL evidence-state rows from the frozen semantic-site matrix) / lexical source tokens of measured_fragment, aggregated across the 44 frozen probes in capability_universe.json using a language-neutral whitespace/punctuation tokenizer (each identifier, keyword, literal, and each individual punctuation/operator glyph counts as one token; string contents count as a single literal token; comments/whitespace excluded).
metric.semantic_density.normalization_note: This shard reports only the Quidra language slice. No cross-language token/fact data is available inside this packet to perform the run's final min-max or comparative normalization across all 10 languages, which is a runner-level aggregation step. The reported 0-100 value is a provisional, explicitly-documented linear transform: normalized_score = round(min(100, raw_density * 100)), where raw_density = total_explicit_local_facts / total_lexical_tokens summed over every probe for which Quidra has a supported fragment. The runner should recompute the final cross-language normalized score once all language shards for metric.semantic_density are merged; the raw aggregate figures below are preserved so that recomputation is possible without re-deriving fragments.

metric.semantic_density.tokenizer_rule: Each keyword, identifier, integer/float/string literal (as one token), and each individual punctuation/operator glyph (including each bracket, dot, comma, and each multi-character operator such as == or += as one token) counts as one lexical token; NEWLINE/INDENT/DEDENT structure, comments, and whitespace are not counted.
